chapter_title: Also concerning the Catechumen; shall he be saved
spiritual_reading:
The mark of one who is fully being formed for regeneration is this: within the person there is truth conjoined with the good it ought to serve, yet it remains as though not one’s own. The whole arrangement of the person’s outward life is held as something temporary and lent for a time, not as a possession. The states of affinity and companionship that surround such a one are regarded as useful only for the present course of reformation, like passing connections permitted for instruction and discipline. These connections will be loosened; and the knowledges, abilities, and outward supports that were employed for a season in the lower degree will be taken away and returned to their proper order. To that person they are like capacities granted for use: one receives them, is aided by them for a time, and afterward yields them back to the order from which they were provided. Therefore the person does not place confidence in outward aids, nor store the heart in them.

When, however, such people are released from the lowest degree of life, they continue according to the ruling love they have acquired, and are raised through an intermediate state into a more interior life. There they are purified in the higher degrees: evils and falsities are separated, and what is mature for heaven is taken up. As works of charity and mercy that have proceeded from genuine good are transferred into what is receptive of heaven, they are changed into many modes of usefulness, freed from what clung to them from the lower degree, and admitted into the living order. In like manner, the interior life of those being formed for regeneration who do not return into another external state is received and elevated according to the same pattern of purification and admission.

Everyone who has received inward expectation and trust, and has made a real distinction between what enlightens the understanding and what obscures and perverts it, and has been granted perception of what makes the inner life truly alive, has also been given conjunction with tranquility from the Divine Wisdom.

As for what remains in such a person, there is examination of what is still separated from heavenly order; and there is painful correction for the evils, and repayment according to their quality. Afterward comes purification, whether in a higher state or in a lower one, according to the measure and character of the person’s actual life. Thus the person is cleansed, renewed in understanding, and invested with what is fitting for heaven. Then the person is brought into a formed spiritual identity that is receptive of wisdom, and is elevated into a state of peace; for whatever a person has loved as the inmost good becomes the person’s abiding possession.

This is from the first proceeding illumination: the Divine truth that gives understanding through wisdom, together with the fullness of the knowledges that are within that wisdom.

fills.notes: The correspondential thread here is that outward associations are temporary and will be loosed; the text needs a transition from present companionship to the certainty of separation. A cognitive verb in the impersonal register fits the oldest substrate: it is knowledge of order, not exhortation.

Required object of “each one … may …” in the sense of companions taking what pertains to their own use and returning it to order; also keeps the focus on temporary fellow-travellers as the ones who withdraw.
The action demanded is the removal of external supports and knowledges when the temporary conjunction ends; “take” matches the later comparison to borrowed vessels that are taken and then returned.

The utensils belong to the same ‘house’ (the temporary external arrangement). This maintains the internal logic: goods of the external life are treated as belonging to that outward state, not to the person.

The image is elevation after purification into rest; ‘glides up’ expresses smooth ascent when impediments have been removed. This matches the spiritual sense: elevation into a state of peace after correction and cleansing.

assessment: Most gaps are tightly constrained by the chapter’s governing correspondence: outward relations and resources are temporary, then withdrawn and returned; purification precedes ascent into rest; illumination proceeds through Mind into fullness of knowledges. Exact particles around ¶3 are less constrained by surviving syntax, but the demanded sequence (certainty of separation → companions withdraw → they take back externals belonging to the temporary house) is recoverable with moderate confidence.
